subject.title: Feature request: cron job auto-retry on failure (--retry-count, --retry-delay)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-job cron retry controls, and if so what public CLI/API/storage contract should they use relative to global `cron.retry`?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix because it creates new user-facing cron settings and persisted API semantics, and there is already a conflicting open implementation candidate.

options.title: Approve additive per-job retry contract
options.body: Define `cron add`/`cron edit`, Gateway schema, persisted job fields, list/status display, defaults, and tests, then repair or replace the linked implementation against that contract.

options.title: Keep global retry only
options.body: Document that global `cron.retry` is the supported recovery knob and close this request after explicitly rejecting per-job retry surface.

options.title: Fold into reason-aware guardrails
options.body: Defer per-job retry controls into the broader reason-aware cron guardrail work tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/14376.

recommendation.title: Approve additive per-job retry contract
recommendation.body: Define `cron add`/`cron edit`, Gateway schema, persisted job fields, list/status display, defaults, and tests, then repair or replace the linked implementation against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged recurring retry behavior and have the strongest recent history on this scheduler path.
